messages:
lia: Heads-up: ran into a flaky upgrade in a customer airgap where multiple nodes pulled the same 6GB model shard concurrently and overloaded the local SSD. We need safer peer-serve coordination patterns.

omar: Oof. Two quick ideas: 1) a cheap "activation lock" per component that prevents activate until verification+quorum. 2) peer-serving should prefer local repo or operator proxy when available to reduce cross-node fetches.

suzie: Activation lock is good. Define states: PENDING -> DOWNLOADING -> VERIFIED -> ACTIVATION_LOCK -> ACTIVATED. Only a node that reached VERIFIED can request lock. Lock can be granted to one node or to a quorum.

dan: Quorum locks complicate apply ordering for multi-component releases. Simpler: single-holder lease for serve + separate activation quorum for switch. Lease TTL short; activation quorum controls final flip.

lia: Agree with dan. Flow: 1) node fetches blob (may be from operator or peer), 2) node verifies sigs, stores resume token, 3) node asks operator for serve-lease (holder id + ttl), 4) requesters use holder to stream, verify chunks locally before commit, 5) when operator triggers rollout, nodes vote to activate based on verified set.

omar: How about operator offline scenarios? Can't rely on central leases. Add fallback "satellite-arbitration" where peers gossip a small signed ballot: holder candidate + nonce + signature. If 2f+1 peers see same holder they respect it.

suzie: Gossip ballot is ok but must be opt-in. Default to operator-first. Add config: `serve_coordination = ["operator", "gossip_satellite"]` with operator default.

dan: Also need safety knobs: max_concurrent_peer_streams (default 3), disk_write_budget_bytes, and `stream_priority` to prefer operator. Avoid thundering herd w/ exponential backoff + jitter before retrying peer fetch.

lia: Telemetry plan: emit metrics named `peerserve.lease_granted`, `peerserve.lease_timeout`, `peerserve.stream_retries_total`, `peerserve.activate_vote_rate`. Also events for `verify_chunk_failed` with blob id and node id.

omar: Security: per-chunk HMAC chain or signature; include chunk index and manifest nonce in signed message so partial streams are verifiable. If any chunk fails verify, requester aborts and reports.

suzie: For resume tokens we should persist them under `/var/lib/redwood/resume/<blobid>` with a small JSON: `{"offset":12345, "manifest_sig":"..."}` — only tokens allowed to be reused if operator manifest sig still valid.

dan: Operator endpoints (minimal): `POST /leases/grant {blob, candidate}` -> {holder, ttl} ; `GET /leases/status?blob=...` ; `POST /leases/force-handoff {blob, new_holder}` authorized. Keep payloads tiny.

lia: Example curl for grant: `curl -X POST $OP /leases/grant -d '{"blob":"sha256:abc...","candidate":"node-3"}'` -> `{"holder":"node-3","ttl":20}`. We'll put auth token header on real impl.

omar: Tests: simulate operator pause + many concurrent clients, assert no duplicate full pulls on same node and that activation only occurs after verification quorum. Add chaos test with random partition.

suzie: Docs: admin runbook for stuck holder: `redwood operator leases inspect <blob>` and `redwood operator leases force-handoff <blob> --reason "holder-unresponsive"`. Force-handoff increments a seatbelt metric to detect frequent ops.

dan: One more: make handoff conservative: candidate nodes wait TTL + 2*backoff_jitter by default before trying to fetch directly. Config knob `handoff_grace_ms`.

ci-bot: CI: added e2e harness job `airgap-peer-serve` + flake threshold. Will post results in #eng-runtime-ci.

lia: Sweet. I'll write RFC draft capturing: operator-first lease, optional gossip ballot, per-chunk signed streams, resume tokens tied to manifest sig, activation quorum separation, telemetry & admin playbook. Dropping first draft in #architecture tomorrow. :rocket:
